advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a boundary case to the enforcing tests: a git version exactly at the floor (2.38.0) must pass, and one just below (2.37.x) must fail, to verify the gate's `sort -V` comparison at its accept/reject discriminator.
evidence: Gate compares via `if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$floor" "$have" | sort -V | head -n1)" != "$floor" ]` with floor `2.38` (_build-and-test.yml:317, .github/git-version-floor.txt)

ABSENCE: neither an exactly-at-floor (2.38.0) nor an adjacent-boundary (2.38.1 / 2.37.x) git version is passed to _run_gate; the equivalence-class boundary of the comparison the change promises to preserve is untested
advisory.finding: The 'enforcement preserved' tests exercise the gate's version comparison only at versions far from the floor (2.99.0 well-above, 2.30.2 well-below), never at the exact-floor boundary (2.38.0, the accept/reject discriminator for `sort -V | head -n1 != floor`) nor just above/below it (2.38.1 / 2.37.x). An off-by-one that made the gate reject exactly-at-floor git, or accept a just-below git, would pass all six new tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test running the gate with git_version="2.38.0" asserting returncode == 0 (exactly-at-floor accepted) and one with git_version="2.37.9" asserting returncode != 0 (just-below rejected), covering the comparison boundary.

coaching.coaching: Add a regression test covering exact-floor boundary coverage in version comparison tests.
